name: tartar sauce
instructions:
Basically [[relish]] suspended in mayonnaise.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- mayonnaise
- dill pickles
- shallots
- parsley
- sugar (adds a lot — see notes)
- lemon juice (LIGHTLY, or at the end — see the failure mode)
- black pepper

=== PROCEDURE ===

Throw it all in a FOOD PROCESSOR — knowing the biggest failure mode is TOO MUCH LIQUID. Go light on the lemon juice, or add it at the end to taste.
notes:
=== THE BIGGEST FAILURE MODE — TOO MUCH LIQUID ===

The food processor makes it easy to end up with a wet, loose sauce. Lemon juice is the main culprit — add it LIGHTLY, or at the END after the texture is set. (Note no pickle juice in this recipe, unlike [[relish]] — the mayo is the suspension and doesn't want loosening.)

=== NEXT TIME — MORE PICKLES, CHUNKIER ===

Next make: FAR MORE PICKLES, and keep them CHUNKY / less processed — pulse the pickles briefly (or hand-chop them in after) rather than riding the processor. The pickle should be the body, in visible pieces.

=== SUGAR IS DOING REAL WORK ===

Sugar adds a lot to balance it — the sweet against the pickle-sour and shallot-sharp is structural, not optional.

=== SHALLOT TOLERANCE — HIGHER THAN RELISH ===

This sauce TOLERATES THE HARSHNESS OF THE SHALLOT more than pure relish does — the mayo buffers it, so you don't have to be as shy. (Corollary for [[relish]]: its biggest failure mode is TOO MUCH SHALLOT/PARSLEY and not enough pickle/celery — noted there too.)

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[relish]]: the suspension-free parent — pickle/celery-forward, shy on shallot.
- [[sauce-andalouse]]: the other mayo-suspension sauce (red pepper direction).
- [[chicken-tenders]] / [[chicken-salad]]: natural targets.
